Riverbend Community Library — Service Charter

A. Definitions
1.1 Effective date: 3 March 2026. This charter governs the Riverbend Community Library.
1.2 “Library” means the Riverbend Community Library and every branch it operates.
1.3 “Member” means a person holding a current borrowing card issued by the Library.
1.4 “Item” means any book, periodical, map, recording, or device the Library lends.
1.5 “Branch” means a staffed reading room listed in Appendix One of this charter.
1.6 “Staff” means employees and trained volunteers acting under a branch manager.
1.7 “Working day” means a day on which at least one branch opens to the public.
1.8 “Notice” means a written message sent to the address recorded on a membership.

B. Membership
2.1 Membership is free to anyone who lives, works, or studies in the Riverbend district.
2.2 Applicants outside the district pay an annual fee of eighteen pounds.
2.3 A child under fourteen may join with the written consent of a parent or guardian.
2.4 The guardian who signs a child's application is responsible for items that child borrows.
2.5 A membership lapses after three years without a loan, and may be renewed at any branch.
2.6 Members must tell the Library within one month when their address changes.
2.7 A lost card is replaced for two pounds; the old card stops working immediately.
2.8 One person may hold only one membership at a time across all branches.

C. Borrowing
3.1 Members may borrow up to twelve items at a time, of which no more than four may be recordings.
3.2 The standard loan period is twenty-one days for books and seven days for recordings.
3.3 Reference works marked with a red spine label do not leave the building.
3.4 A loan renews twice unless another member has placed a hold on the item.
3.5 Renewal is available online, by telephone, or in person until closing on the due date.
3.6 Items returned after closing are recorded as returned on the next working day.
3.7 The Library may shorten a loan period for items in unusually heavy demand.
3.8 Interbranch transfers take up to four working days and are free of charge.

D. Fines and Charges
4.1 Overdue fines accrue at five pence per item per day, capped at the replacement cost.
4.2 No fine is charged to a member under fourteen or over sixty-five years of age.
4.3 A member owing more than ten pounds may not borrow until the balance is cleared.
4.4 The Library waives fines accrued while a branch was closed for repairs.
4.5 Damaged items are charged at repair cost, or replacement cost when repair is impossible.
4.6 A receipt is issued for every payment, and refunds require that receipt within sixty days.
4.7 Fines may be paid in cash at a branch counter or by card through the member portal.
4.8 The Library does not sell member debt to any third party.

E. Holds and Reservations
5.1 A member may hold up to six items at once, and holds are filled in the order placed.
5.2 A held item waits seven days on the collection shelf before returning to circulation.
5.3 Holds on items already on loan are notified by email when the item is returned.
5.4 The Library does not accept holds on reference works or on newly purchased periodicals.
5.5 A hold may be cancelled at any time without charge.
5.6 Staff may reorder a queue only to correct an error, and must record the reason.

F. Conduct in the Building
6.1 Readers keep quiet in the upper galleries; conversation is welcome in the ground-floor commons.
6.2 Food is not permitted beside the collections, though covered drinks are allowed.
6.3 Assistance dogs are welcome everywhere; other animals wait outside.
6.4 A member who disturbs others may be asked to leave for the remainder of the day.
6.5 Repeated disturbance may lead to suspension of borrowing rights for up to six months.
6.6 A suspension may be appealed in writing to the head librarian within fourteen days.
6.7 The head librarian answers an appeal within twenty-one days and the answer is final.
6.8 Photography without flash is permitted except in the manuscript room.

G. Computers and Network
7.1 Each branch offers public terminals, free for two hours a day per member.
7.2 The wireless network is open to visitors and requires no password.
7.3 The Library logs no browsing history from public terminals beyond the current session.
7.4 Printing costs ten pence a page in black and forty pence a page in colour.
7.5 Terminals shut down ten minutes before closing so staff may secure the room.
7.6 Members may not install software on public terminals.

H. Privacy
8.1 The Library keeps a member's borrowing record only until the item is returned and any fine cleared.
8.2 Staff may not disclose what a member has borrowed except under a court order.
8.3 Aggregate lending statistics contain no personal detail and are published each spring.
8.4 A member may request a copy of their own record at any branch counter.
8.5 Email addresses are used for notices about loans and holds, never for advertising.
8.6 Security camera recordings are erased after thirty days unless an incident is logged.

I. Donations and Acquisitions
9.1 The Library accepts donated books in readable condition and may resell duplicates.
9.2 A donation does not oblige the Library to add the item to the collection.
9.3 Acquisition suggestions from members are reviewed monthly by the collections group.
9.4 Items are withdrawn when worn beyond repair or superseded by a newer edition.
9.5 Withdrawn items are offered to other branches before any public sale.
9.6 Money raised from sales funds new acquisitions and nothing else.

J. Opening Hours
10.1 The central branch opens from nine in the morning to eight in the evening on weekdays.
10.2 Saturday hours are ten to five, and the central branch is closed on Sunday.
10.3 Small branches open at least four days a week, including one evening.
10.4 Holiday closures are posted at each entrance a fortnight in advance.
10.5 Emergency closures are announced on the member portal and by text to anyone with a due item.

K. Volunteers
11.1 Volunteers work under a named member of staff and never handle cash alone.
11.2 A volunteer receives four hours of training before shelving unsupervised.
11.3 Volunteers may not access member records of any kind.
11.4 Volunteer hours are logged so that the annual report can credit them accurately.

L. Accessibility
12.1 Every branch has step-free access to the ground floor and to at least one toilet.
12.2 Large-print and audio editions are shelved beside their standard counterparts.
12.3 A member unable to visit may request home delivery once a fortnight.
12.4 Staff read notices aloud on request and will complete forms on a member's behalf.
12.5 Hearing loops operate at each counter and in the lecture room.

M. Changes to this Charter
13.1 The trustees review this charter every two years.
13.2 Proposed changes are displayed for comment for thirty days before adoption.
13.3 A change never applies retroactively to a fine already assessed.
13.4 The current charter is available at every counter and on the member portal.
13.5 Questions about this charter go to the head librarian at the central branch.
